title: Patch-Seq Internal Solution with Biocytin
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
materials: RNase Zap or RNase Away Decontaminant (Invitrogen AM9780, Thermo Scientific 53225-514 or equivalent)
Potassium Chloride (2 M KCl, molecular biology grade) (Thermo Fisher Scientific AM9640G)
4-(2-Hydroxyethyl) piperazine-1-ethanesulfonic acid, N-(2-Hydroxyethyl) piperazine-N′-(2-ethanesulfonic acid) (1 M HEPES, BioPerformance certified) (C8H18N2O4S) (Sigma H3537 or equivalent)
Ethylene Glycol-bis (2-aminoethylether)-N,N,N’,N’-Tetraacetic Acid (EGTA, molecular biology grade) ([-CH2OCH2CH2N(CH2CO2H)2]2) (Sigma E3889 or equivalent)
Glycogen, RNA grade (Thermo Fisher Scientific R0551)
Dye of choice from the following list:
Cascade Blue Hydrazide, Trisodium Salt (Thermo C687)
Steriflip 0.22 µm (Thermo Fisher SCGP00525 or Millipore SE1M179M6)

steps.title: Prepare EGTA Stock Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a 192 mM EGTA stock solution.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 3.65 g of EGTA in 32 ml nuclease-free water in a labeled 50 ml conical tube.
Add 4M KOH dropwise until EGTA is fully dissolved (up to 6 ml may be required).
Bring the final volume to 50 ml with nuclease-free water.
Store at 4°C for up to 60 days and label with expiration date.

steps.title: Prepare Fluor Dye Stock
steps.instruction: Prepare a ~10 mM stock of the desired dye.

substeps.instruction: Add 175 µl of nuclease-free water to 1 mg of the desired dye in a 1.5 ml lo-bind tube.
Aliquot 25 µl of the stock into PCR strips.
Store at -20°C for up to 6 months and label with expiration date.

steps.title: Set Up Preparation Environment
steps.instruction: Prepare the workspace in an RNase-free hood.

substeps.instruction: Place an RNase-free stir bar in a 100 ml glass beaker designated for Patch-Seq Internal Solution.
Set up the stir plate in the hood.

steps.title: Combine Internal Solution Components
steps.instruction: Prepare 80 ml of Internal Solution in an RNase-free hood while stirring at a high setting (300 RPM or higher).

substeps.instruction: Measure 60 ml of nuclease-free water using a graduated cylinder and add to the beaker.
Place the beaker in a glass dish or tray containing a mixture of wet and dry ice.
Slowly add 2.06 g of K-Gluconate.
Add 160 µl of 2 M KCl using a P200 pipettor.
Add 800 µl of 1 M HEPES using a P1000 pipettor.
Slowly add 40.56 mg of ATP-Mg.
Slowly add 12.56 mg of GTP-Na.
Slowly add 204.08 mg of Sodium Phosphocreatine.
Slowly add 400 mg of biocytin (use brief periods of vortexing if necessary to dissolve).
Add 82 µl of 192 mM EGTA stock solution using a P200 pipettor.
Add 80 µl of 20 mg/ml Glycogen solution using a P200 pipettor.
Continue stirring until all chemicals are fully in solution.

steps.title: Adjust pH and Volume
steps.instruction: Calibrate the pH and finalize the volume of the solution.

substeps.instruction: Measure pH using a calibrated pH meter in a fume hood.
Adjust pH to 7.3 by adding 4N KOH in 20 µl increments (discard prep if pH is overshot).
Remove the stir bar using a magnetic stir bar remover.
Adjust the final volume to 80 ml with nuclease-free water using a graduated cylinder or calibrated beaker marks.

steps.title: Adjust Osmolarity
steps.instruction: Measure and adjust the osmolarity of the solution using a Vapro osmometer.

substeps.instruction: Measure a 10 µl sample. Target range is 220-230 mOsm.
If osmolarity is too high, add nuclease-free water.
If osmolarity is too low, add a volume (X) of 1 mg/ml K-Gluconate solution (calculated by provided equation).
Confirm the correct osmolarity has been reached and record the volume of water/K-Gluconate added.

steps.title: Filter and Aliquot Base Solution
steps.instruction: Sterilize the solution and store in aliquots.

substeps.instruction: Filter the solution through a Steriflip 0.22 µm filter system attached to a Gast vacuum pump via Tygon tubing.
Aliquot 5 ml quantities into 5 ml microcentrifuge tubes (approx. 15 tubes per batch).
Label tubes as 'Internal solution with Biocytin'.
Store aliquots at -80°C for up to 60 days.

steps.title: Prepare Final Working Solution
steps.instruction: Every six weeks, prepare working aliquots by adding inhibitors and dyes.

substeps.instruction: Thaw five to eight 5 ml aliquots of internal solution.
Add 62.5 µl of RNase Inhibitor (40 U/µl) to 5 ml of internal solution using a P200 pipettor.
Add 25 µl of the requested Fluor stock (~10 mM) to the solution using a P200 pipettor.
Filter the combined solution using an Agros PVDF filter and a BD 10ml syringe into a new 15 ml BD Falcon tube.
Repeat filtration with a fresh set of filters to ensure the solution is particle-free.
Measure osmolarity of a 10 µl sample; acceptable range is 305-320 mOsm.

steps.title: Quality Control and Final Storage
steps.instruction: Verify solution quality and store in small aliquots.

substeps.instruction: Test for clogging: Load 1 µl into a glass capillary pipette, place in IVSCC rig, and monitor under 40x guidance for blockages. Repeat 10-15 times for 2 minutes each.
Aliquot 200 µl into 1.5 ml LoBind tubes (37-39 tubes per 10 ml) using a P1000 pipette.
Store filled PCR strips in a freezer box at -80°C.
Label the box with reagent name, date, preparer's initials, and expiration date.
Record date of preparation, lot numbers of all components, and osmolarity in the reagent prep notebook.

steps.title: Cleanup and Decontamination
steps.instruction: Clean equipment and workspace to maintain RNase-free conditions.

substeps.instruction: Dispose of excess reagent into the municipal sewer system.
Wash the stir bar with RNase Away and rinse with nuclease-free water.
Wipe down the RNase-free hood with RNase Zap or RNase Away Decontaminant, followed by 70% EtOH.
Remove tip waste bucket, dispose of tips, re-wipe the hood with RNase Zap/Away and 70% EtOH, then return the bucket.
